title: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit upright in a firm chair with feet flat on the floor. Slowly lift your heels off the ground as high as comfortable, pressing through the balls of your feet. Hold for two seconds, then lower your heels back down with control.
purpose: Promotes plantarflexion strength, improves ankle mobility, and aids lower-limb venous return without weight-bearing stress.

position_cues.0: Seated with back support; small range.

title: Seated Toe Taps & Shin Lift
instructions: Keep your heels planted on the floor and pull your toes up toward your shins as far as possible. Hold briefly at the top, then tap your feet back down in a steady, controlled rhythm.
purpose: Targets the tibialis anterior muscle to reduce toe-drag risk during gait and improve ankle dorsiflexion.

title: Standing Calf Raise (Chair)
instructions: Stand tall behind a stable chair, lightly gripping the backrest for balance. Rise up onto your toes smoothly, holding your body straight. Pause at the top, then gently lower your heels back to the ground.
purpose: Builds functional gastrocnemius/soleus strength in full weight-bearing while maintaining a stable balance support.

title: Supported Loaded Calf Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a chair back or wall with hands supported. Step one leg back, keeping the heel flat on the floor and the back knee fully straight. Lean forward slightly at your hips until you feel a gentle stretch in the back calf; hold statically without bouncing.
purpose: Increases gastrocnemius length and ankle dorsiflexion range of motion, reducing Achilles tendon stiffness.

title: Seated Pelvic Tilt & Kegel
instructions: Sit comfortably in your chair. Gently pull your belly button toward your spine while drawing up your pelvic floor muscles (as if stopping the flow of urine). Hold for 3 to 5 seconds while breathing normally, then relax completely.
purpose: Engages the pelvic floor musculature and deep abdominal stabilizers to support lumbo-pelvic alignment and bladder control.

title: Seated Trunk Rotation
instructions: Sit tall with feet flat. Turn your upper torso smoothly to one side, bringing your hand across to rest on the opposite thigh or chair arm. Keep your hips stationary and look slightly over your shoulder; pause, return to center, and repeat on the other side.
purpose: Enhances thoracic spinal rotation, alleviates stiffness in the mid-back, and supports functional twisting during daily activities.

position_cues.0: Seated with back support; small range.

title: Supine Glute Bridge + Core Lock
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on a firm surface. Engage your stomach muscles to keep your spine neutral, then press through your heels to raise your hips until aligned with your thighs. Squeeze your buttocks at the top, then lower down slowly.
purpose: Restores posterior chain activation (gluteus maximus) while stabilizing the lumbar spine to prevent low-back pain.

title: Seated Diagonal Woodchopper
instructions: Sit up tall and clasp your hands together near one shoulder. Bring your arms down and across your body toward your opposite hip in a smooth diagonal motion, keeping your core engaged. Reverse the movement back to the starting position.
purpose: Trains diagonal rotatory patterns involving the internal and external obliques for cross-body functional movement.

position_cues.0: Seated with back support; small range.

title: Seated Isometric Glute Squeeze
instructions: Sit toward the front edge of your seat with your back straight. Firmly squeeze your buttock muscles together as tightly as comfortable. Hold this contraction for 5 seconds while maintaining steady breathing, then release.
purpose: Encourages neurological re-education and isometric strength in the gluteal muscles without joint loading.

title: Standing Hip Extension (Chair)
instructions: Stand holding a chair back for support. Keep your chest elevated and your knee straight, then slowly extend one leg directly backward behind you. Focus on squeezing your buttock rather than arching your lower back, then return smoothly.
purpose: Strengthens the gluteus maximus and hip extensors while reinforcing single-leg stance stability on the stance leg.

title: Supported Chair Sit-to-Stand
instructions: Scoot forward in your chair, place your feet shoulder-width apart, and lean slightly forward at your hips. Push through your heels to stand straight up (using armrests for assistance if needed). Pause, then slowly lower yourself back down into the chair.
purpose: Rebuilds quadriceps and gluteal force production necessary for transfers, sit-to-stand transitions, and stair navigation.

position_cues.4: Slow tempo or pause at bottom.

title: Standing Side Hip Abduction
instructions: Stand tall facing a chair back with hands placed lightly on top. Keeping your toes pointing forward and your torso upright, lift one leg straight out to the side. Pause briefly, then lower the leg back down without leaning your body.
purpose: Activates the gluteus medius to maintain lateral pelvic stability during the stance phase of walking.

title: Seated High-Knee Holds
instructions: Sit erect with good posture. Lift one knee up toward your chest as high as comfortable without slumping backward. Hold the elevated position for 2 to 3 seconds, then lower your leg under control.
purpose: Targets the iliopsoas and rectus femoris to improve hip flexion clearance during gait swing phase.

position_cues.0: Seated with back support; small lift.

title: Seated Resisted Leg Raise
instructions: Sitting tall, place one or both hands gently on your thigh just above the knee to apply light downward resistance. Press your leg up against your hands to lift your knee, engaging the muscles on top of your thigh before lowering.
purpose: Builds quadriceps strength and knee extension control required for leg stability.

position_cues.0: Seated with back support; small range.

title: Standing Chair Marching
instructions: Stand close to a sturdy chair, gripping the back for safety. Alternate lifting your knees up toward waist level in a controlled marching rhythm, maintaining an upright posture throughout.
purpose: Enhances dynamic single-leg balance, hip flexor endurance, and reciprocal limb coordination.

title: Static Supported Step Lunge
instructions: Hold a firm chair back and take a step backward into a staggered stance. Keep your back heel raised and your torso upright. Bend both knees slightly to lower your body vertically into a small, controlled lunge, then press back up through your front foot.
purpose: Lengthens the hip flexors and improves functional strength and stability in a split-stance base of support.

title: Seated Lat Stretch & Reach
instructions: Sit straight and reach one arm up toward the ceiling. Lengthen through your torso, then lean gently to the opposite side until you feel a soft stretch down your side. Hold for a few deep breaths, then return to upright.
purpose: Decompresses the thoracic spine and lengthens the latissimus dorsi to relieve shoulder restriction and mid-back tightness.

position_cues.0: Seated with back support; small reach.

title: Wall Slides / Arm Ladder
instructions: Stand facing a wall with forearms or fingertips resting against it. Slowly slide your arms up the wall as high as your shoulder flexibility allows without arching your lower back. Hold at the top briefly, then slide back down.
purpose: Promotes scapular upward rotation, overhead mobility, and thoracic extension.

title: Supported Wall Push-Offs
instructions: Stand an arm's length away from a wall, placing your palms flat at shoulder height. Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the wall in a controlled manner, keeping your body in a straight line, then press firmly back to the start.
purpose: Builds closed-kinetic-chain upper body strength (pectoralis, anterior deltoid, triceps) with minimal shoulder impingement risk.

title: Seated Goalpost Squeeze
instructions: Raise your arms out to the sides with elbows bent at 90 degrees (like a goalpost). Draw your shoulder blades back and together, squeezing gently between your upper back muscles. Hold for 3 seconds, then release.
purpose: Strengthens the middle trapezius and rhomboids to counteract rounded shoulder posture (kyphosis).

title: Seated Rhythm March & Arm Drive
instructions: Sit tall away from the backrest. March your feet in a steady, energetic rhythm while swinging your arms back and forth in opposition. Focus on deep, rhythmic breathing as you maintain the movement.
purpose: Boosts low-impact cardiovascular conditioning and upper/lower limb coordination in a safe seated position.

title: Supine Spinal Twist
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms out to the sides. Slowly lower both knees together to one side while keeping both shoulders grounded on the floor. Hold gently, then use your core to return to center and repeat on the other side.
purpose: Improves lumbar spine mobility, gently stretches chest muscles, and reduces paraspinal muscular tension.

title: Standing Side-Step Taps
instructions: Stand behind a chair with hands resting lightly on the frame. Step your left foot out to the side, tap your right foot next to it, then step back to the right. Continue side-stepping continuously with steady control.
purpose: Improves lateral movement capacity, hip abductor engagement, and weight-shifting balance.

title: Supported Deep Squat Hold
instructions: Hold securely onto a sturdy support or chair back. Lower your hips down and back into a comfortable squat depth while keeping your heels flat and chest lifted. Hold the isometric position for 3 to 5 seconds before pressing back up to standing.
purpose: Preserves lower-extremity joint mobility (hips, knees, ankles) and promotes end-range leg strength.
